preamble: The phonetic transformation from a voiceless alveolar affricate ([ts]) to a voiceless glottal fricative ([h]) represents a significant sound change, typically categorized as a form of lenition or debuccalization. This shift involves a weakening of the articulatory effort, moving from a complex sound with a complete closure and fricative release at the alveolar ridge to a simpler fricative produced solely at the glottis.

examples.note: Proto-Tupi-Guarani *ts became /h/ in Guarani (Mbya lost it entirely: kwee), while Tupinambá has /s/.

Tocantins Asurini belongs to Rodrigues and Cabral's subgroup IV, where *ts and *tʃ merged as /h/ independently of the Guarani development in subgroup I; the same merger as /h/ or zero characterizes subgroups VI–VIII (Kayabí, Kamayurá, Wayampi and others).

sources: Carvalho, F. O. de (2022). On the Guaranian evidence for two Proto-Tupi-Guarani affricates. Journal of Language Relationship, 20(1), 81–112. https://doi.org/10.31826/jlr-2022-201-207
